title: Network Delay Time
description: Given a directed network of n nodes with travel times on edges and a source node k, return the time for a signal from k to reach all nodes, or -1 if some node is unreachable.

reference.use_case: Determining how long a signal sent from one node takes to reach every other node in a network with per-link delays, or whether some nodes cannot be reached.
system_examples: OSPF and IS-IS routing protocols — each router computes shortest paths over link costs
Navigation apps (e.g. Google Maps) — fastest-route computation over road networks
Gossip/broadcast protocols — estimating worst-case propagation time of an update across a cluster
reference.explanation: With non-negative edge weights, Dijkstra's algorithm with a min-heap finds the earliest arrival at every node in O(E log V); the answer is the maximum of those times, or -1 if any node is unreachable. Shortest paths are the foundation of link-state routing and navigation.
